static_gap_analysis.text:
`repricing_gap_analysis` answers "where in time does my balance sheet reprice, and how does the running total build up?" It returns the gap for each time bucket (rate-sensitive assets minus rate-sensitive liabilities) plus the cumulative gap, which is what drives net interest income sensitivity. It also accepts optional `bucket_labels` so you can name the buckets.

`static_gap_analysis` answers "how do my rate-sensitive assets compare with my rate-sensitive liabilities at this point in time, assuming a frozen balance sheet?" It gives the per-bucket gap and also a gap ratio, which is total rate-sensitive assets divided by total rate-sensitive liabilities. Both take the same two inputs, `bucket_assets` and `bucket_liabilities`.

In short, the first emphasises the cumulative gap across buckets, while the second emphasises the point-in-time view and the overall ratio.

explain.text: `repricing_gap_analysis` (Repricing Gap Analysis) calculates the repricing gap for each time bucket, defined as rate-sensitive assets minus rate-sensitive liabilities. It also returns the cumulative gap, the running sum of those bucket gaps, which drives net interest income (NII) sensitivity. You supply `bucket_assets` and `bucket_liabilities`, the amounts repricing in each bucket, and can optionally add `bucket_labels` to name the buckets. It suits ALM and balance-sheet work where you want to see how repricing mismatches build up across time.

when.text:
Use Repricing Gap Analysis (`repricing_gap_analysis`) when you want to see how rate-sensitive assets and liabilities line up across time buckets:

- You already have rate-sensitive assets and liabilities allocated to repricing buckets and want the gap per bucket (assets minus liabilities).
- You want the cumulative gap, which drives net interest income (NII) sensitivity.
- You want a clear view of where repricing mismatches sit along the time ladder, with optional `bucket_labels` to name the buckets.
- Your inputs are `bucket_assets` and `bucket_liabilities` for each bucket.

Related function: `repricing_maturity_profile` allocates balances into repricing-time buckets, so it fits if you still need to build the buckets before running the gap.
